messages:
alex_chu: quick dump from today's microbatch sweep — streaming chat vs sync completions. found a weird latency stair-step around MB=4 for streaming traffic, p99 blows up compared to MB=2.

devon: can you paste the numbers?

alex_chu: sure, short table from canary (streaming route):
```
MB=1: p95=42ms  p99=120ms  qps=180
MB=2: p95=48ms  p99=130ms  qps=320
MB=4: p95=75ms  p99=420ms (!) qps=610
MB=8: p95=210ms p99=720ms qps=1100
```

alex_chu: non-streaming completions for same model have smoother curve (p99 grows gradually), spike is primarily on streaming path.

maria_g: interesting. any kernel selector logs around the p99 events?

alex_chu: yes — selector is flipping to generic kernel when KV footprint crosses ~64MB, looks like a thrash + KV miss penalty. excerpt: 
```
[selector] ts=1719999958 model=redwood-8b-v2 seq=1024 kv_bytes=78MB -> kernel=generic_gemm fallback (orig=xformers_opt)
[perf] tail_latency_increase: +280ms, kv_miss_count++
```

timothy: so KB: streaming requests keep long-lived KV, but microbatching at MB=4 causes worker to accept a mix of new prefixes and warm KV -> eviction -> read-from-disk -> kernel fallback.

devon: can we confirm eviction logs / kv-hit-ratio at MB boundaries?

alex_chu: already pulled traces: kv_hit_ratio drops from 99%@MB2 to ~86%@MB4 during peak. also saw kernel change events correlated with tail spikes.

maria_g: quick mitigation idea: split pools by traffic pattern. streaming pool: cap MB at 2-3 and prefer kernels with lower memory working set; completions pool: higher MB. that keeps latency SLO for chat.

timothy: agree. also we can try a kernel-hint: prefer_fp16_matmul for streaming to reduce kv footprint, might avoid fallback. small perf delta but improves tail.

devon: what's the throughput/cost hit if we limit MB for streaming?

alex_chu: measured delta on canary for chat-heavy routes: limiting streaming MB to 2 => p99 down from 420ms->140ms, p95+/-5ms, qps capacity drops ~8% so cost up ~7-9% for same traffic. tradeoff seems acceptable for interactive apps.

ops-bot: canary deploy: mb-heuristic-v2 -> eng-runtime-canary (started 1719999980) :rocket:

maria_g: long-term fixes: 1) make kernel selector aware of KV residency (avoid heavy kernels when kv_live_ratio < 0.95), 2) add prefetcher for KV during streaming warmup, 3) metricize kernel_changes as span tags so evals can correlate with quality/latency.

alex_chu: plan posted: run 48h canary with split pools + kernel-hint experiment, gather p50/p95/p99 per-route and kernel-change counts, then decide. will also run a synthetic workload to reproduce steady-state knee.

timothy: assignable tasks? I can take the selector change PR and tests.

alex_chu: thanks. devon can we have SRE add an alert rule for sudden kernel fallback rate > 0.5%/min for streaming pools? that should catch regressions early.

devon: yep will add alert and a dashboard with p99 vs kernel-fallback-rate.

maria_g: :thumbsup: good triage.

alex_chu: final note — for the follow-up we'll capture a small flamegraph during an MB=4 spike (kernel + kv io stack) and attach to the ticket.

ops-bot: ticket created: RW-3245 "mb stair-step: streaming tail from kernel/fallback interaction" (link: https://tracker.redwood.ai/RW-3245)
